messages:
oncall-bot: paging SRE oncall — high error-rate and latency spike observed in ap-southeast-1 for inference endpoints. error-rate 5.1% (5m), p50 latency 480ms -> alert threshold exceeded. auto-escalation P1.

inc-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0423-APAC-CANARY. Triage channel: #incidents. Runbook: /runbooks/canary-rollback.

ops-jordan: ack — I'm on, collecting dashboards. Can anyone confirm last deploy window and which variant was shifted?

eng-mike: we kicked off a weighted blue->green shift for model-serving v2.3.1 at 2026-04-23T08:12:00Z. Intended split: green=20% -> 60% now. Canary target = ap-southeast-1 only.

sre-jen: seeing 502s and increased tail latency from downstream kv-cache misses. Error traces point to mismatch between edge routing and origin pool (some requests routed to green where kernels aren't warmed).

ops-jordan: checking DNS and edge resolution — ap-sg-region shows inconsistent answers across resolvers. Some resolvers still return blue endpoints, some green. TTLs are 300s but edge caches may have longer. That would cause sticky sessions to cold-start on green.

support-lina: getting multiple customer pings: "model responses time out / partial outputs" for customers in APAC. Raising CS priority; notifying impacted accounts list now.

eng-mike: likely root cause: rollout orchestration incremented traffic too fast while green nodes still warming KV caches and loading quantized weights. We should pause and roll back.

ops-jordan: can we flip feature flag kill-switch? We have FF service: feature=canary-apac-v2.3.1.

eng-mike: I'll trigger kill-switch now. Command: ```bash
curl -X POST https://flags.internal/api/v1/flags/canary-apac-v2.3.1/kill -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN"
```

ops-jordan: executed at 08:16:23Z — flags service returned 200. Traffic should start shifting back to blue immediate at routing layer. inc-bot: please log rollback event.

inc-bot: Rollback event logged by ops-jordan at 2026-04-23T08:16:23Z. Traffic policy reverted to baseline (blue primary).

net-chris: requested network flush to reduce DNS caching skew: pushing low-level cache-bust to edge and requested upstream resolver nxdomain purge. Command to run on edges: ```bash
for node in $(cat apac-edge-list); do ssh $node "sudo service edge-dns flush"; done
```

devex-ali: sending CDN cache-bust for routing headers + prefix KV keys to warm blue nodes: new warmup job queued (priority=high).

sre-jen: metrics are improving — error-rate back to 0.8% (5m) and p50 down to ~120ms, but p99 still elevated. Keeping monitors on.

support-lina: telling CS: most customers should see stability now; will update impacted list and coordinate follow-ups.

pm-simran: please capture customer-impact summary for postmortem: affected region, percent of traffic, top impacted customers, time-to-stable, and mitigation steps.

ops-jordan: creating mitigation timeline in the incident doc now. Current plan: 1) keep rollback active until we validate warm-start strategy; 2) reduce canary step size and add explicit kernel-warm hooks; 3) add DNS weight reconciliation check to rollout jobs; 4) add automated TTL flush to edge on canary flip.

eng-mike: will open a PR with a conservative rollout config and a warmup pre-hook for model-serving. Also adding a gating check that validates origin pool readiness (kv cache hit-rate > 85%) before increasing weight.

inc-bot: handoff: oncall SRE shift change incoming in 25m — @sre-jen please acknowledge handoff to next oncall.

sre-jen: acknowledged. @ops-jordan I'll stay as incident lead through handoff and then pair with next oncall for follow-up.

ops-jordan: final note: DNS propagation mismatch was the operational multiplier — rollout automation assumed uniform resolver behavior. Action item: update rollout docs and add explicit resolver reconciliation step.

inc-bot: incident severity reduced to P2 at 2026-04-23T08:45:15Z. Postmortem requested in 72h.

sre-jen: closing update — leaving open for postmortem artifacts and runbook edits. Thanks all for quick responses. :thumbsup:
